# Psalm 22 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** For the choirmaster. According to The Doe of the Dawn. A psalm of David.

**2** My God, my God, why have You forsaken me? Why are You so far from saving me, from the words of my groaning?

**3** O my God, I cry by day, but You do not answer, and by night, but I find no rest.

**4** Yet You are holy, enthroned on the praises of Israel.

**5** In You our fathers trusted; they trusted, and You delivered them.

**6** To You they cried and were rescued; in You they trusted and were not put to shame.

**7** But I am a worm and not a man, scorned by mankind and despised by the people.

**8** All who see me mock me; they make mouths at me; they wag their heads:

**9** "He trusts in the LORD; let Him deliver him; let Him rescue him, for He delights in him!"

**10** Yet You are He who took me from the womb; You made me trust You at my mother's breasts.

**11** On You was I cast from my birth, and from my mother's womb You have been my God.

**12** Be not far from me, for trouble is near, and there is none to help.

**13** Many bulls encompass me; strong bulls of Bashan surround me;

**14** they open wide their mouths at me, like a ravening and roaring lion.

**15** I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint; my heart is like wax; it is melted within my breast.

**16** My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue sticks to my jaws; You lay me in the dust of death.

**17** For dogs encompass me; a company of evildoers encircles me; they have pierced my hands and my feet.

**18** I can count all my bones — they stare and gloat over me.

**19** They divide my garments among them, and for my clothing they cast lots.

**20** But You, O LORD, do not be far off! O You my help, come quickly to my aid!

**21** Deliver my soul from the sword, my precious life from the power of the dog!

**22** Save me from the mouth of the lion! You have rescued me from the horns of the wild oxen!

**23** I will tell of Your name to my brothers; in the midst of the congregation I will praise You:

**24** You who fear the LORD, praise Him! All you offspring of Jacob, glorify Him, and stand in awe of Him, all you offspring of Israel!

**25** For He has not despised or abhorred the affliction of the afflicted, and He has not hidden His face from him, but has heard, when he cried to Him.

**26** From You comes my praise in the great congregation; my vows I will perform before those who fear Him.

**27** The afflicted shall eat and be satisfied; those who seek Him shall praise the LORD! May your hearts live forever!

**28** All the ends of the earth shall remember and turn to the LORD, and all the families of the nations shall worship before You.

**29** For kingship belongs to the LORD, and He rules over the nations.

**30** All the prosperous of the earth eat and worship; before Him shall bow all who go down to the dust, even the one who could not keep himself alive.

**31** Posterity shall serve Him; it shall be told of the Lord to the coming generation;

---
## LOGOS Translation Notes

- **22:1**: The most important psalm in Christian theology. More NT citations and allusions come from Psalm 22 than from any other psalm.

- **22:22-31**: The dramatic shift from agony to praise at v.22 is the psalm's structural hinge. Suffering gives way to testimony, testimony to universal worship.

— LOGOS
